review: 509.3e-2: Seifer was controlled by the defending player B, so its trigger (a creature attacking one of Seifer's controller's opponents) could never fire for A's attacker; moved Seifer to A, fixed its goad-trigger target, and stated the trigger resolution.
509.3e-1: blocks_one left the two-attacker damage assignment of the base in force; delta now states the Giant blocks the first Grizzly Bears and assigns all its damage to it.

509.3g-1: blocker_removed differed from the base in two facts (a block and an Unsummon); Unsummon on Grizzly Bears now happens in every variant, the plain blocked variant is dropped, and blocked_then_removed changes only the block.

509.4-1: base was labelled does_not_fire although the rule's effect (the token never counts as having blocked) happens in it; relabelled fires. A does_not_fire case cannot exist, since every creature put onto the battlefield blocking never blocked.
509.1b-3: flying_before_block jumped from an illegal declaration to an unblocked attacker; expected now states the declaration is undone and B declares no blockers.

scenarios.title: A tapped creature cannot be chosen as a blocker

setup.notes: In the tapped_blocker variant Hill Giant is entered as {"card": "Hill Giant", "tapped": true}.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
In the declare blockers step B declares Hill Giant as a blocker of Grizzly Bears.
No spells or abilities are used.

variants.label: untapped_blocker
variants.expected: The declaration is legal: untapped Hill Giant is a legal blocker for Grizzly Bears, which is attacking B. Grizzly Bears becomes blocked by Hill Giant.

variants.label: tapped_blocker
variants.delta: B's Hill Giant starts the turn tapped.
variants.expected: Hill Giant is not a legal blocker: the declaration is illegal. Grizzly Bears is not blocked by it.

scenarios.forge_notes: The tapped state of a non-active player's creature must be set as a puzzle starting condition.

scenarios.title: A creature without flying or reach cannot block an attacker with flying
decisions: A attacks B with Wind Drake.
In the declare blockers step B declares Grizzly Bears as a blocker of Wind Drake.
No spells or abilities are used.

variants.label: ground_blocker
variants.expected: The declaration is illegal: Grizzly Bears has neither flying nor reach, so the evasion restriction of Wind Drake is disobeyed. Wind Drake is not blocked by it.

variants.label: reach_blocker
variants.delta: B declares Giant Spider (reach) as the blocker instead of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: The declaration is legal: Giant Spider has reach. Wind Drake becomes blocked by Giant Spider.

scenarios.title: A creature that can block only flyers cannot block a ground attacker
decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
In the declare blockers step B declares Cloud Sprite as a blocker of the attacker.
No spells or abilities are used.

variants.label: ground_attacker
variants.expected: The declaration is illegal: Cloud Sprite can block only creatures with flying and Grizzly Bears has none. Grizzly Bears is not blocked.

variants.label: flying_attacker
variants.delta: A attacks B with Wind Drake instead of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: The declaration is legal: Wind Drake has flying and Cloud Sprite has flying. Wind Drake becomes blocked by Cloud Sprite.

scenarios.title: An evasion ability gained after a legal block does not undo the block
decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
B declares Hill Giant as a blocker of Grizzly Bears.
A casts Aerial Maneuver targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping both Plains, with priority in the declare blockers step; both players pass and it resolves.
Combat damage is dealt; no other spells or abilities are used.

variants.label: flying_after_block
variants.expected: Hill Giant stays a blocker: Grizzly Bears (3/3, flying, first strike) remains blocked by it. In the first-strike damage step Grizzly Bears deals 3 damage to Hill Giant, which is destroyed before dealing damage. B's life stays 20.

variants.label: flying_before_block
variants.delta: A casts Aerial Maneuver on Grizzly Bears during the declare attackers step, before blockers are declared; B then tries to declare Hill Giant as a blocker.
variants.expected: Declaring Hill Giant as a blocker is illegal: Grizzly Bears has flying and Hill Giant does not. The declaration is undone and B declares no blockers; Grizzly Bears is unblocked and deals 3 damage to B (life 17); Hill Giant survives.

scenarios.title: A creature that blocks each combat if able must block when it can
decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
In the declare blockers step B declares no blockers.
No spells or abilities are used.

variants.label: no_block_declared
variants.expected: The declaration is illegal: Razorgrass Screen is untapped, able to block Grizzly Bears, and must block, so declaring no blockers obeys fewer requirements than possible.

variants.label: block_declared
variants.delta: B declares Razorgrass Screen as a blocker of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: The declaration is legal. Grizzly Bears becomes blocked by Razorgrass Screen.

variants.label: screen_tapped
variants.delta: B's Razorgrass Screen starts the turn tapped.
variants.expected: Declaring no blockers is legal: a tapped creature cannot block, so no requirement can be obeyed. Grizzly Bears is unblocked and deals 2 damage to B (life 18).

scenarios.forge_notes: The requirement check against the maximum obeyable set is implemented by Forge's blocking-requirement validation; the tapped state of a non-active creature is a puzzle starting condition.

scenarios.title: A block requirement is obeyed as far as restrictions allow
decisions: A attacks B with Boggart Brute (menace).
In the declare blockers step B declares both Razorgrass Screen and Dune Beetle as blockers of Boggart Brute.
No spells or abilities are used.

variants.label: both_block
variants.expected: The declaration is legal: two creatures block the menace attacker and the blocking requirement of Razorgrass Screen is obeyed. Boggart Brute becomes blocked by both.

variants.label: neither_blocks
variants.delta: B declares no blockers.
variants.expected: The declaration is illegal: the requirement of Razorgrass Screen could be obeyed without disobeying menace (both blocking), but is not.

variants.label: only_screen_blocks
variants.delta: B declares only Razorgrass Screen as a blocker.
variants.expected: The declaration is illegal: it violates the menace restriction, which needs two or more blockers.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's handling of must-block requirements that conflict with menace should be confirmed.

scenarios.title: A declared blocker becomes a blocking creature until it is removed from combat
decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
B declares Hill Giant as a blocker of Grizzly Bears.
Neither player casts a spell or activates an ability unless a variant says so; combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: blocker_stays
variants.expected: Hill Giant is a blocking creature of Grizzly Bears: Grizzly Bears deals 2 damage to Hill Giant (2 damage marked, survives) and Hill Giant deals 3 damage to Grizzly Bears, which is destroyed.

variants.label: no_block
variants.delta: B declares no blockers.
variants.expected: Hill Giant is not a blocking creature and takes no damage. Grizzly Bears is unblocked and deals 2 damage to B (life 18).

variants.label: blocker_removed
variants.delta: After blockers are declared, A casts Unsummon targeting Hill Giant, tapping Island, and it resolves.
variants.expected: Hill Giant returns to B's hand and is no longer a blocking creature. Grizzly Bears remains blocked, deals no damage and takes no damage (B's life stays 20).

scenarios.title: A blocked creature stays blocked after its blockers leave combat
decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
B declares Hill Giant as a blocker of Grizzly Bears (in the never_blocked variant B declares no blockers).
With priority in the declare blockers step A casts Unsummon targeting Hill Giant, tapping Island; it resolves.
Combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: blocked_then_blocker_removed
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears remains a blocked creature although Hill Giant returned to B's hand. It has no trample, so it deals no combat damage and B's life stays 20.

variants.label: never_blocked
variants.delta: B declares no blockers.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is an unblocked creature and deals 2 damage to B (life 18) even though Hill Giant is returned to B's hand.

scenarios.title: A trigger on being blocked triggers when blockers are declared
decisions: A attacks B with Deepwood Tantiv.
B declares Grizzly Bears as a blocker of Deepwood Tantiv (in the unblocked variant B declares no blockers).
Both players pass priority so any trigger resolves.

variants.label: blocked
variants.expected: Deepwood Tantiv's trigger fires on the declaration of blockers; it resolves and A gains 2 life (22).

variants.label: unblocked
variants.delta: B declares no blockers.
variants.expected: No trigger fires; A's life stays 20.

scenarios.title: Block triggers are on the stack before the active player gets priority
decisions: A attacks B with Deepwood Tantiv.
B declares Grizzly Bears as a blocker of Deepwood Tantiv (in the unblocked variant B declares no blockers).
When A first receives priority in the declare blockers step, A casts Shock targeting player B, tapping Mountain.
Both players pass until the stack is empty.

variants.label: blocked
variants.expected: When A gets priority, Deepwood Tantiv's trigger is already on the stack, so Shock is put above it. Shock resolves first (B life 18), then the trigger resolves (A life 22).

variants.label: unblocked
variants.delta: B declares no blockers.
variants.expected: No trigger is on the stack when A gets priority; the stack holds only Shock. Shock resolves (B life 18) and A's life stays 20.

scenarios.title: A 'whenever this creature blocks' ability triggers once even if it blocks several creatures
decisions: A attacks B with both Phyrexian Walkers.
B declares Clockwork Beetle as a blocker of both Phyrexian Walkers (it can block an additional creature).
Beetle assigns its 2 damage to the first Walker; combat damage is dealt and the end of combat step passes.

variants.label: blocks_two
variants.expected: Beetle's blocks trigger fires once and creates one delayed trigger; at end of combat one +1/+1 counter is removed. Beetle stays on the battlefield with one counter (1/1).

variants.label: blocks_one
variants.delta: B declares Clockwork Beetle as a blocker of only one Phyrexian Walker.
variants.expected: The trigger fires once; at end of combat one counter is removed. Beetle stays with one counter (1/1).

variants.label: no_block
variants.delta: B declares no blockers.
variants.expected: No blocks trigger fires. Beetle keeps both counters (2/2). B's life stays 20.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge fires Mode$ Blocks once per blocker, so the single-trigger result with two blocked attackers needs confirming.

scenarios.title: A 'whenever this creature blocks a creature' ability triggers once per attacker blocked
decisions: A attacks B with both Phyrexian Walkers.
B declares Brimaz, King of Oreskos as a blocker of both Phyrexian Walkers (it can block an additional creature).
B puts the two Brimaz triggers on the stack in either order; each token blocks the attacker its trigger names. Both players pass until the stack is empty.

variants.label: blocks_two
variants.expected: Brimaz triggers twice. B gets two 1/1 Cat Soldier tokens with vigilance, one blocking each Phyrexian Walker.

variants.label: blocks_one
variants.delta: B declares Brimaz as a blocker of only one Phyrexian Walker.
variants.expected: Brimaz triggers once. B gets one Cat Soldier token, blocking that Walker.

variants.label: no_block
variants.delta: B declares no blockers.
variants.expected: Brimaz does not trigger; B gets no token.

scenarios.title: A 'becomes blocked' ability triggers once per combat however many creatures block
decisions: A attacks B with Deepwood Tantiv.
B declares one Grizzly Bears as a blocker of Deepwood Tantiv (the two_blockers variant declares both).
Both players pass so any trigger resolves. A assigns Deepwood Tantiv's 2 combat damage to the first Grizzly Bears.

variants.label: one_blocker
variants.expected: The trigger fires once and A gains 2 life (22).

variants.label: two_blockers
variants.delta: B declares both Grizzly Bears as blockers of Deepwood Tantiv.
variants.expected: The trigger still fires only once: A gains 2 life (22), not 4.

variants.label: unblocked
variants.delta: B declares no blockers.
variants.expected: No trigger fires; A's life stays 20.

scenarios.title: A 'becomes blocked by a creature' ability triggers once for each blocking creature
decisions: A attacks B with Cave Tiger (2/2).
B declares one Grizzly Bears as a blocker of Cave Tiger (other variants declare differently).
Both players pass until the stack is empty at the declare blockers step.

variants.label: one_blocker
variants.expected: Cave Tiger triggers once and becomes 3/3 until end of turn.

variants.label: two_blockers
variants.delta: B declares both Grizzly Bears as blockers of Cave Tiger.
variants.expected: Cave Tiger triggers twice and becomes 4/4 until end of turn.

variants.label: token_blocks_too
variants.delta: B declares Brimaz as the blocker of Cave Tiger (no Grizzly Bears block).
variants.expected: Brimaz's trigger creates a Cat Soldier token that enters blocking Cave Tiger. Cave Tiger triggers for Brimaz and again for the token, and becomes 4/4 until end of turn.

variants.label: unblocked
variants.delta: B declares no blockers.
variants.expected: Cave Tiger does not trigger and stays 2/2.

scenarios.forge_notes: Whether Forge fires AttackerBlockedByCreature for a creature put onto the battlefield blocking needs confirming.

scenarios.title: A trigger on blocking two or more creatures needs that count when blockers are declared
decisions: A attacks B with both Grizzly Bears.
B declares Lairwatch Giant as a blocker of both Grizzly Bears (it can block an additional creature).
The Giant assigns 2 first-strike damage to the first Grizzly Bears and 3 to the second. No spells or abilities are used.

variants.label: blocks_two
variants.expected: Lairwatch Giant's trigger fires and it gains first strike until end of turn. Both Grizzly Bears are destroyed in the first-strike damage step and the Giant takes no damage.

variants.label: blocks_one
variants.delta: B declares Lairwatch Giant as a blocker of only the first Grizzly Bears (the Giant assigns all its damage to it).
variants.expected: The trigger does not fire; the Giant has no first strike. The blocked Grizzly Bears is destroyed in the regular damage step while the Giant takes 2 damage and survives; the other Grizzly Bears is unblocked and deals 2 damage to B (life 18).

scenarios.title: A trigger on an attacker becoming blocked by two or more creatures needs that count
decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears; Seifer, Balamb Rival does not attack.
Seifer's attack trigger targets the first Phyrexian Walker; both players pass and it resolves (the Walker is goaded).
B declares both Phyrexian Walkers as blockers of Grizzly Bears.
Both players pass so any trigger resolves. A assigns 1 damage to each Phyrexian Walker. No other spells or abilities are used.

variants.label: two_blockers
variants.expected: Seifer's trigger fires and Grizzly Bears gains deathtouch until end of turn. Both Phyrexian Walkers are destroyed by 1 damage each and Grizzly Bears takes no damage.

variants.label: one_blocker
variants.delta: B declares only one Phyrexian Walker as a blocker; A assigns all 2 damage to it.
variants.expected: The trigger does not fire; Grizzly Bears has no deathtouch. The Phyrexian Walker (0/3) takes 2 damage and survives.

scenarios.forge_notes: Seifer's goad trigger fires because A attacks B; goad does not restrict blocking.

scenarios.title: A block trigger with a characteristic condition checks the characteristic when blocked
decisions: A attacks B with Dread Specter.
B declares Dune Beetle as a blocker of Dread Specter.
Combat damage is dealt and the end of combat step passes. No other spells or abilities are used unless a variant says so.

variants.label: black_blocker
variants.expected: Dune Beetle is black, so Dread Specter's trigger does not fire. Both creatures survive combat (Dune Beetle has 2 damage, Dread Specter 1).

variants.label: recolored_before_block
variants.delta: In the beginning of combat step A activates Distorting Lens targeting Dune Beetle and chooses green.
variants.expected: Dune Beetle is nonblack when it blocks, so the trigger fires and Dune Beetle is destroyed at end of combat. Dread Specter survives.

variants.label: recolored_after_block
variants.delta: After blockers are declared A activates Distorting Lens targeting Dune Beetle and chooses green.
variants.expected: Dune Beetle was black when it blocked, so the trigger does not fire even though it is now green. Dune Beetle survives combat.

scenarios.title: An 'attacks and isn't blocked' ability needs no blockers declared
decisions: A attacks B with Crypt Cobra.
B declares no blockers.
With priority in the declare blockers step, after any trigger is on the stack, A casts Unsummon targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Island; both players pass until the stack is empty.
Combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: unblocked
variants.expected: Crypt Cobra's trigger fires and B gets 1 poison counter. Grizzly Bears returns to B's hand. Crypt Cobra deals 3 damage to B (life 17).

variants.label: blocked_then_removed
variants.delta: B declares Grizzly Bears as a blocker of Crypt Cobra.
variants.expected: The trigger does not fire; B has no poison counters. Grizzly Bears returns to B's hand, Crypt Cobra stays blocked, deals no damage and B's life stays 20.

scenarios.title: A creature put onto the battlefield blocking never 'blocked'
decisions: A attacks B with Phyrexian Walker.
B declares Brimaz as a blocker of Phyrexian Walker (the other variants differ in the declaration).
Both players pass until the stack is empty.

variants.label: brimaz_blocks
variants.expected: Carnage Gladiator triggers once for Brimaz; B loses 1 life (19). Brimaz's trigger creates a Cat Soldier token blocking Phyrexian Walker; Gladiator does not trigger for the token.

variants.label: brimaz_and_bears_block
variants.delta: B declares Brimaz and Grizzly Bears as blockers of Phyrexian Walker.
variants.expected: Carnage Gladiator triggers for each declared blocker; B loses 2 life (18). The token that enters blocking does not add a trigger.

variants.label: no_block
variants.delta: B declares no blockers.
variants.expected: No block triggers fire; B's life stays 20 and no token is created.

scenarios.title: A creature put onto the battlefield blocking an attacker that left combat is not blocking
decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
B declares Brimaz as a blocker of Grizzly Bears; Brimaz's trigger is put on the stack naming Grizzly Bears.
In the attacker_removed variant A responds by casting Unsummon targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Island.
Both players pass until the stack is empty.

variants.label: attacker_still_attacking
variants.expected: The Cat Soldier token enters blocking Grizzly Bears.

variants.label: attacker_removed
variants.delta: In response to Brimaz's trigger A casts Unsummon targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Island.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears returns to A's hand. The Cat Soldier token enters the battlefield but is not blocking any creature.

scenarios.title: A creature put onto the battlefield blocking ignores block restrictions
decisions: A attacks B with Arlinn's Wolf (can't be blocked by creatures with power 2 or less).
B declares Brimaz (power 3) as a blocker of Arlinn's Wolf.
Both players pass until the stack is empty.

variants.label: brimaz_blocks
variants.expected: The declaration is legal. Brimaz's trigger creates a 1/1 Cat Soldier token that enters blocking Arlinn's Wolf although its power is 1.

variants.label: lions_blocks
variants.delta: B declares Savannah Lions (power 2) as the blocker instead of Brimaz.
variants.expected: The declaration is illegal: a declared blocker with power 2 or less disobeys the restriction. Arlinn's Wolf is not blocked.
